correctness.rationale: For any fixed isolated vertex, other iid points are uniformly distributed in the single complementary interval of length L=1-2r, and any path through the excluded arc has length at least 2r>r. Integrating a pair of uniform points on that interval proves the conditional remaining-edge probability min(1,1-(1-r/L)^2). Multiplying the conditional-minus-unconditional edge mean by nPr(isolated) yields the exact formula. On r<1/3 the sign polynomial Q_n=-4+(3n+10)r-8nr² is strictly negative for n<=5 and has one relevant root for n>=6; on r>=1/3 the linear sign factor n-2-2nr has one root iff n>=6. All root identities, strict inequalities, endpoint transitions, and n=6 exception are covered by proof; verify.py passes 5781 algebraic/sign/simulation corroboration assertions.

value.rationale: The sharp six-point threshold is a motivated qualitative dependence transition between two elementary network sparsity statistics, not an arbitrary finite enumeration: isolation can be positively correlated with the total edge count despite ordinarily reducing incident edges. The conditional confinement mechanism explains how increased clustering among remaining vertices outweighs lost incident edges, gives an exact radius interval and both unique roots for every n>=6, and a complete negative classification for smaller graphs.
